Main.sentence: An airstrike , air strike , or air raid  is an ___E:offensive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offensive_(military))___ operation against ___E:ground U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground)___ or ___E:sea surface U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_surface)___ targets carried out by ___E:aircraft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft)___ .

Air strikes are delivered from aircraft such as ___E:military balloons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_balloon)___ , ___E:airships U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airship)___ , ___E:attack aircraft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_aircraft)___ , ___E:bombers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bomber)___ , ___E:gunships U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunship)___ , ___E:attack helicopters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_helicopter)___ and ___E:attack drones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Attack_drones&action=edit&redlink=1)___ .

The official definition of an airstrike includes all sorts of targets, including enemy air targets, but in popular usage the term is usually narrowed to a ___E:tactical U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_tactics)___ (small-scale) ___E:strafing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strafing)___ , ___E:missile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missile)___ strike or ___E:tactical bombing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tactical_bombing)___ on a specific ___E:army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army)___ , ___E:militia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Militia)___ or ___E:naval U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval)___ position, as opposed to a larger, more generalized and indiscriminate attack against an entire area such as ___E:carpet bombing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpet_bombing)___ and ___E:strategic bombing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_bombing)___ .

Weapons used in an airstrike can range from ___E:aircraft-mounted U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_artillery)___ ___E:direct-fire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct-fire)___ ___E:cannons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_cannon)___ and ___E:machine guns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_gun)___ , ___E:rockets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_(weapon)#Air-launched)___ and ___E:air-to-surface missiles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air-to-surface_missile)___ , to various types of ___E:aerial bombs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerial_bomb)___ (both ___E:unguided U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unguided_bomb)___ and ___E:guided U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guided_bomb)___ ), ___E:glide bombs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glide_bomb)___ , ___E:air-launched cruise missiles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air-launched_cruise_missile)___ , and even ___E:directed-energy weapons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed-energy_weapon)___ such as ___E:laser weapons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_weapon)___ .

In ___E:close air support U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close_air_support)___ , air strikes are usually controlled by ___E:trained observers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_air_control)___ on the ground for coordination with ground troops and intelligence in a manner derived from ___E:artillery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artillery)___ tactics.

The first large scale air raid occurred during ___E:World War I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I)___ in 1915, when ___E:London U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London)___ was bombed by 15 German ___E:Zeppelin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeppelin)___ dirigibles at night.

Since the residents of London, and many of its defenders, were asleep, a loud warning system for air raids made sense, leading to the creation of the ___E:air raid siren U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_defense_siren)___ .

It was not until ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ that the ___E:Oxford English Dictionary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_English_Dictionary)___ first records usage of the term "air strike",  which remained two separate words for some time thereafter.

The ___E:Second World War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War)___ also saw the first development of ___E:precision-guided munitions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precision-guided_munition)___ , which were fielded successfully by the Germans, and contributed to the modern sense of air "strike", a precision targeted attack as opposed to a ___E:strafing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strafing)___ run or ___E:area bombing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Area_bombing)___ .

The importance of precision targeting cannot be overstated: by some statistics, over a hundred raids were necessary to destroy a point target in World War 2; by the ___E:Persian Gulf War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf_War)___ , the ___E:U.S. Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Air_Force)___ was able to release to media precise footage of television- or radar-guided bombs directly hitting the target without significant collateral damage (using, for example, the ___E:LANTIRN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LANTIRN)___ pod). ___E:Paul Fussell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Fussell)___ noted in his seminal work ___E:The Great War and Modern Memory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Great_War_and_Modern_Memory)___ the popular 20th century tendency to assume an errant bomb hitting a church, for example, was completely deliberate and reflective of the inherent evil of the enemy; over time, expectations for reduced collateral damage have increased to the point that developed countries engaging in war against less technologically advanced countries approach near-zero in terms of such damage.

In the ___E:Malayan Emergency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayan_Emergency)___ of the 1950s, British and Commonwealth ___E:Avro Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avro_Lincoln)___ heavy bombers, ___E:de Havilland Vampire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Havilland_Vampire)___ fighter jets, ___E:Supermarine Spitfires U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supermarine_Spitfire)___ , ___E:Bristol Brigands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_Brigand)___ , ___E:de Havilland Mosquitos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Havilland_Mosquito)___ , and a host of other British aircraft were used in Malaya in operations against guerillas.
However, the humid climate played havoc with the Mosquito's wooden airframe, and they were soon deployed elsewhere.
This period also marked the last combat deployment of British Spitfires.

During the Vietnam War, airstrikes and their doctrine were adjusted to fit the jets, like the ___E:North American F-100 Super Sabre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_F-100_Super_Sabre)___ , ___E:Republic F-105 Thunderchief U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_F-105_Thunderchief)___ , ___E:Douglas A-4 Skyhawk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_A-4_Skyhawk)___ , and ___E:McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonnell_Douglas_F-4_Phantom_II)___ , which were entering the U.S.A.F. and U.S.N. inventory.

These aircraft could fly faster, carry more ordnance, and defend themselves better than the ___E:F-4U Corsair U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vought_F4U_Corsair)___ and ___E:North American P-51 Mustang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_P-51_Mustang)___ fighters that fought during the Korean War, albeit at the cost of the R&D of the aircraft itself, the weapons, and, most important to the man on the ground, fuel and loiter time, though this situation was slightly alleviated with the introduction of aircraft like the ___E:Cessna A-37 Dragonfly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cessna_A-37_Dragonfly)___ , ___E:LTV A-7 Corsair II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LTV_A-7_Corsair_II)___ , and ___E:Lockheed AC-130 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_AC-130)___ gunships.

Today, airstrike terminology has extended to the concept of the ___E:strike aircraft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_aircraft)___ , what earlier generations of military aviators referred to as ___E:light bombers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_bomber)___ or ___E:attack aircraft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_aircraft)___ .

With the near-complete air supremacy enjoyed by developed nations in undeveloped regions, fighter jets can often be modified to add strike capability in a manner less practicable in earlier generations.

Airstrikes can be carried out for strategic purposes outside of general warfare. ___E:Operation Opera U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Opera)___ was a single eight-ship Israeli airstrike against the Iraqi ___E:Osirak nuclear reactor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuwaitha_Nuclear_Research_Center)___ , criticized by world opinion but not leading to a general outbreak of war. Such an example of the ___E:preventive strike U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preventive_war)___ has created new questions for international law.

Airstrikes, including airstrikes by drones, were extensively used during the ___E:Gulf War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War)___ , ___E:War on Terror U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_terror)___ , ___E:War in Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Afghanistan_(2001%E2%80%932021))___ , ___E:Iraq War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War)___ , ___E:First Libyan Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Libyan_Civil_War)___ , ___E:Syrian Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_civil_war)___ , ___E:Iraqi Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Iraq_(2013%E2%80%932017))___ , ___E:Yemeni Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemeni_Civil_War_(2014%E2%80%93present))___ , ___E:2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine)___ and the ___E:Gaza war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war)___ .

Airstrike campaigns often cause the deaths of ___E:non-combatants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-combatant)___ , including civilians.   ___E:International law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_law)___ apply the principles of military necessity , distinction , and proportionality .

These principles emphasize that an attack must be directed towards a ___E:legitimate military target U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legitimate_military_target)___ and the harm caused to non-combatant targets must be proportional to the advantage gained by such attack.
Many modern military aircraft carry ___E:precision-guided munitions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precision-guided_munition)___ , which military sources promote as decreasing civilian deaths.
